copies.headline: Noah Needs Receivers, Not Another Patriot
copies.body:
Receiver decides this and it isn't close: Adam's top three go 50 to Noah's 39, and that's with Chris Olave questionable in a Saints game totaling 45.5 — if Olave sits, Jalen Coker and Rome Odunze are real options, which is more than Noah can say. Noah's WR room is Garrett Wilson as a 7.5-point underdog in Foxborough, Michael Wilson chasing points in a 51.5-total blowout in LA, a questionable Josh Downs, and Jordyn Tyson on IR. Jaxon Smith-Njigba in a 40.5-total game in Denver is the one spot Adam has to sweat.
Everywhere else it's a coin flip on paper — QB +1, RB +2, TE +1 — but Adam's floor is the difference. He's 5-0, 154.5 a game, 49-6 all-play, and hasn't scored under 142 all year. Noah is last in the league in points and all-play, with a Patriots stack that mostly works if New England covers a 7.5-point spread in a 43.5 game. That's a ceiling play, not a plan.

copies.headline: Logan's Roster Runs Out Of Receivers
copies.body:
John wins this at tight end and the margins stack from there. Brock Bowers is questionable, which barely matters when Trey McBride is the backup plan — Arizona is a 12.5-point dog in a 51.5-total game, so he'll be catching passes all fourth quarter. Logan counters with Isaiah Likely in a Giants game totaling 45.5. The Rams stack is the real problem: Puka Nacua and Kyren Williams in a 51.5-point game against a defense that can't stop either, plus Matthew Stafford over Deshaun Watson in a 41.5-total slog against Baltimore. That's four positional edges and none of them are close.
Logan's receiver room is the tell. Tetairoa McMillan at 16 in a 38.5-total game in Philadelphia is the ceiling, and behind him it's Luther Burden III and Germie Bernard. Justin Jefferson at zero isn't walking through that door. Jeremiyah Love questionable, Zach Charbonnet out, and Joe Burrow still a decoration on the bench — this roster needs everything to break right, and 112.3 a game says it hasn't.

copies.headline: Christian's 1-4 Is A Clerical Error
copies.body:
Christian is 1-4 with the fourth-best scoring average and a 31-24 all-play, which is just math being rude; Isaac is 2-3 averaging 104 with a 16-39 all-play, which is the opposite problem. The positional edges line up for Christian everywhere but running back. Jordan Love and CeeDee Lamb both sit in the 53.5-total Cowboys-Packers game, Brandon Aubrey is kicking in it too, and George Kittle gets Washington in a 51.5 with San Francisco favored by 7.5 — that's a 15-point tight end against Isaac's Dalton Kincaid at 8, with Hockenson questionable and nothing else behind him.
Isaac's counter is backfield volume: Javonte Williams, Cam Skattebo, J.K. Dobbins and a questionable Saquon Barkley against Christian's Tuten-plus-hobbled-Kamara group, worth roughly eight. Not enough. Jameis Winston as a 1.5-point home dog in a 45.5 is fine, but Ja'Marr Chase on bye guts the receiver room, leaving Nabers and McLaurin to carry it. Christian's floor is the problem — 103.1 last week — but Isaac hasn't cracked 122 all year.

copies.headline: Grant's 3-2 Is a Costume
copies.body:
Both teams are 3-2, and only one of them has earned it. Leif is third in scoring at 131.7 and third in all-play at 33-22; Grant is ninth in points at 108.3 with a 21-34 all-play and 1.1 wins of luck propping up the record. The backfield is where this gets decided. Christian McCaffrey and Derrick Henry project 43 against Grant's best two at 28, and Grant's top option is a questionable Quinshon Judkins behind Tony Pollard, whose Titans are seven-point dogs in a 44.5-total game in Indianapolis. McCaffrey gets San Francisco laying 7.5 with a 51.5 total. That's not a close comparison.
Quarterback adds seven more: Josh Allen in a 53.5-point game in Las Vegas versus Kirk Cousins, with nothing behind him but a zeroed-out Kyler Murray. Grant's path is the receiver room, which is genuinely fine — Christian Watson in a 53.5 Packers-Cowboys game and Zay Flowers can match Leif's 44 — plus a small tight end edge. But Mike Evans and Davante Adams both sit in 51.5-total spots, and Leif only needs them to be ordinary. Stefon Diggs questionable is the one soft spot, and Chris Godwin covers it.

copies.headline: Mitchell's Backfield Is A Rounding Error
copies.body:
The running backs decide this and it isn't close. CJ's top two, Jonathan Taylor (19) against Tennessee as a seven-point home favorite and Emanuel Wilson or Chuba Hubbard at 15, beat Mitchell's best pair by 17. That's Tyjae Spears, who's questionable, and George Holani in a 40.5-total game in Denver. Jahmyr Gibbs is on a bye and Jordan Mason is on IR, so the depth behind the depth is Najee Harris. Mitchell wins receiver by five with Matthew Golden and Nico Collins, but Collins is in a 42.5-point game in Jacksonville and DJ Moore carries a tag too.
Mitchell's live path is the Dallas-Green Bay total of 53.5 — Dak Prescott at 17 in the week's best shootout, plus Golden on the other sideline. That's real ceiling. But CJ matches at quarterback with Tyler Shough and holds a roster with four startable receivers, so Mitchell needs the ceiling, not just the edges.

copies.headline: Kaleb's Quarterback Problem Shows Up Again
copies.body:
This is quarterback and little else. Peter gets Lamar Jackson at 19, questionable tag and all, in a Ravens-Browns game with a 41.5 total that won't ask much of him; Kaleb counters with Justin Herbert at 12, down 8.5 at Kansas City in a 42.5-point game, with Jared Goff on a zero behind him. Even a chase-mode fourth quarter in Arrowhead doesn't close that gap when Herbert's only reliable target, Ladd McConkey, is questionable. Receiver is actually Kaleb's strength — Drake London, Carnell Tate, Tre Tucker and Keenan Allen give him 38 to Peter's 37 — but Peter's group is held together by George Pickens in a 53.5-total Cowboys-Packers game, which is the single best environment on either roster.
Running back tilts Peter by five on Bijan Robinson alone, in a 51.5-total Falcons game, against Ashton Jeanty catching garbage work as a 5.5-point dog. Peter's depth behind Bijan is ugly — Kyle Monangai questionable, Josh Jacobs day-to-day — and he's running +1.5 lucky. Kaleb's +1.1 lucky and 10th in scoring with a 38 percent all-play. Thin beats thinner.

intro: Leif at Grant is the one worth watching: two 3-2 teams separated by a tiebreaker, with Leif carrying a slim edge into a game where either side's RB2 decides it. The bigger gap is Peter at Kaleb, where the 4-1 roster has the healthier top-end talent and Kaleb's depth has been getting exposed since the bye weeks started. Adam is favored again at 5-0, which at this point is less a matchup and more a weekly reminder that Noah's 1-4 was built the hard way.
